messages.author: 7f14ee7fbacc9635
messages.subject: Why Not Bootstrap
parts:
Hi All

I have a basic question. Bootstrapping is used when the data is not normal. However, in AMOS when we need to assess mediation, we have to check direct and indirect effects.

However, in Lavaan, we do not need to bootstrap (although we can) for indirect effects.

Why?

Kind Regards

messages.author: bc810b1d0900407f
messages.subject: Re: Why Not Bootstrap
parts: > Bootstrapping is used when the data is not normal.
May I know why you think so?
> However, in AMOS when we need to assess mediation, we have to check direct and indirect effects.

I think you meant checking the check boxes to ask for the direct and indirect effects in the output. I am not sure what you meant by "However". In lavaan, we also need to tell lavaan we want to estimate indirect effect. We even need to form the product of path coefficients ourselves. AMOS enumerates all possible indirect effects automatically. In this aspect, AMOS is more convenient.

Nevertheless, AMOS does *not* estimate indirect effects along some paths automatically (e.g., in a parallel mediation model); we need to form the parameters ourselves:

http://amosdevelopment.com/features/user-defined/user-defined-simple/Tutorial2/pdf/SimpleUserDefined2.pdf

This is quite inconvenient. It is much easier to specify the indirect effects to estimate in lavaan if we are interested in individual pathways.
> However, in Lavaan, we do not need to bootstrap (although we can) for indirect effects.

The indirect effect in SEM is a user-defined parameter (e.g., the product of two path coefficients). By default, lavaan uses the delta-method to form the CIs for user-defined parameters, including the indirect effect. Do you imply that delta-method CI is better than bootstrapping CI for an indirect effect?

As far as I know, AMOS cannot produce delta-method CI for user-defined parameters (I may be wrong because there are a lot of functions in AMOS that I am not familiar with). In lavaan, we can request delta-method CI (default) or bootstrapping CI. I think it is a question of which CI is better rather than which program is better for estimating an indirect effect. The default method may or may not be the best method.

I hope I did not misunderstand your question.

-- Shu Fai
